findings.explanation: AuditEvent is the only Key Vault log category. SecretSet is an operationName, and there is no SecretRotate secret operation: rotation operations exist only for keys (KeyRotate, KeyRotateIfDue). A secret rotation appears as SecretSet or SecretUpdate (a new version), often preceded by SecretNearExpiryEventGridNotification.
findings.quote: Azure Key Vault diagnostic categories SecretSet and SecretRotate via Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Azure
findings.suggested_fix: Collect Key Vault category=AuditEvent and treat operationName IN (SecretSet, SecretUpdate) on the target secret as rotation evidence. Remove SecretRotate here and in detailedImplementation Lane C.

findings.explanation: RotateSecret only records that a rotation was requested. Secrets Manager writes separate service events (RotationStarted, RotationSucceeded, RotationFailed, RotationAbandoned) that show the outcome. Counting RotateSecret as last_rotation_ts marks failed rotations as compliant, which is exactly the failure that Case K in detailedImplementation describes.
findings.quote: sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail RotateSecret and PutSecretValue for AWS Secrets Manager
findings.suggested_fix: In dataSources and detailedImplementation Lane B, use eventName=RotationSucceeded (with PutSecretValue plus UpdateSecretVersionStage for manual rotations) as rotation evidence, and RotationFailed/RotationAbandoned as failure signals.

findings.explanation: No Splunk-built 'Splunk Add-on for HashiCorp Vault' exists. The Splunkbase listing is the HashiCorp-built 'HashiCorp Vault App for Splunk' (5093). The trailing text makes the AWS TA the collector for every lane, including Vault, Azure and the gateway lanes.
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for HashiCorp Vault — Splunk Add-on for Amazon Web Services (Splunkbase 1876)
findings.suggested_fix: List each lane's real collector: Splunk Add-on for AWS (1876) for CloudTrail, Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Azure (3757) or Event Hub for Key Vault, Splunk Add-on for Google Cloud Platform (3088), HashiCorp Vault App for Splunk (5093) or a UF file monitor for the Vault audit device, and HEC for gateway logs.

findings.explanation: Repository guides use hashicorp:vault:audit (identity-platforms-pam-sso.md) or vault:audit:json (cert-pki.md) for the same feed. The Vault audit device nests fields as request.path and request.operation, not the top-level path or operation that the description implies.
findings.quote: index=security sourcetype=vault:audit HashiCorp Vault audit JSON
findings.suggested_fix: Align the sourcetype with the guides (hashicorp:vault:audit). State that rotation evidence comes from request.operation IN (create, update) on request.path matching the KV path of the LLM credential.

findings.explanation: The fenced SPL in Step 3 uses mean(), but the spl field uses avg(). The text claims an exact match that does not hold, so copy-paste readers get a different search from the catalogue one.
findings.quote: Fenced SPL must match the spl JSON field exactly: ... | eventstats mean(key_age_days) AS bu_mean_age
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the fenced block with the exact spl field content, or drop the 'must match exactly' claim.

findings.explanation: CIM data model acceleration and tstats come from the free Splunk Common Information Model add-on (1621), not Enterprise Security. Nothing in the SPL needs ES.
findings.quote: Splunk Enterprise Security — Optional CIM Authentication and Change tstats acceleration
findings.suggested_fix: Remove Enterprise Security from premiumApps and name the CIM add-on as the prerequisite for Change acceleration.

findings.explanation: The SPL only queries Change. Authentication appears only as a future enrichment in dataModelAcceleration.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep Change only, or say that Authentication is not used by the current search.

findings.explanation: A verified status with reviewer 'catalog-team' conflicts with SPL whose AWS lane and Change join always return nothing (see the firewalled flags) and with wrong vendor operation names. No SME sign-off is evident.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade to draft until the search has been run against real CloudTrail, Key Vault and Vault audit data.

findings.explanation: The GCP audit methodName is google.cloud.secretmanager.v1.SecretManagerService.AddSecretVersion; 'SecretVersion Add' is not a searchable value.
findings.quote: forward SecretManager SecretVersion Add events through the Splunk Add-on for GCP

firewalled_field_flags.issue: coalesce(requestParameters.secretId, ...) is not quoted. In eval, '.' is the concatenation operator, so the expression evaluates to null and every AWS row becomes 'aws_unscoped', which is then nulled. Use 'requestParameters.secretId' in single quotes. See https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/SearchReference/Eval.

The CIM Change root dataset is All_Changes. tstats ... FROM datamodel=Change WHERE nodename=Change BY Change.object returns no rows, so change_recent is always 0. Use nodename=All_Changes and All_Changes.object.

The AWS lane keys on eventName=RotateSecret/PutSecretValue instead of RotationSucceeded. The Azure lane filters on 'secretrotate' and the undefined token 'npr'. The Vault lane reads top-level operation and path instead of request.operation and request.path. Each lane can misstate when rotation happened.

gateway_last_used is taken per logical_key_id alias, not per credential version. A gateway still using the old version after rotation will still advance gateway_last_used, so gateway_cutover_gap cannot detect the stale-key case the title promises without a credential fingerprint or version field.

summary: The detailedImplementation explains the cosmetic-rotation and gateway-cutover problem well, but several product facts are wrong. The UC cites a non-existent Splunk Vault add-on, Azure Key Vault operations that do not exist, and AWS RotateSecret as proof of a completed rotation. The SPL has field-reference defects that silently empty the AWS and CIM Change lanes.
